newsitem.title: UK: UK sees new international telecom licences in Dec.
newsitem.headline: UK sees new international telecom licences in Dec.

text.p: The British government said on Monday that it hoped to issue the first operating licences to new competitors in the international telecoms market in December.
In a statement, the Department of Trade and Industry asked for comments on a new draft version of the licence, which is aimed at increasing competition in company communications.
"Competition will reduce prices for U.K. consumers, encourage more inward investment and boost our position as Europe's leading telecoms hub," science and technology minister Ian Taylor said.

Taylor said the government's aim, first set out in March, is to create a regulatory regime which cuts costs to industry but gives telecoms regulator Oftel the power to act against anti-competitive practices.
The latest draft proposals retain provisions "to counter any possible abuse of the current accounting mechanisms by monopoly telecommunications operators based overseas," the DTI said.
Some 46 companies applied for an international facilities license in the first wave of applications in June, and the DTI said it hoped to issue licenses to all by the end the year.
